case_title: Parveen Kumar v. The State of Himachal Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498-A; IPC s.306; Evidence Act s.113A (presumption as to abetment of suicide)
weapon: Aluminium phosphide tablets (insecticide) consumed by the victim
evidence_type: Circumstantial (proof of prior complaints and cruelty, presumption under s.113A); documentary (FIR, complaints, maintenance petition, daily diary entry, post-mortem referral); oral evidence of the victim's brother and two defence neighbours
aggravating_circumstances: Victim had filed three cases against the accused during her lifetime; death within seven years of marriage; accused did not inform the victim's parents immediately after the incident
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498-A IPC; two years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000 with default clause; acquitted under s.306 IPC
high_court_outcome: Accused's appeal against s.498-A conviction dismissed; State's appeal against s.306 acquittal allowed and accused convicted under s.306 IPC
offence_finally_established: IPC s.498-A (cruelty by husband) and IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide)
neutral_facts: The accused married the victim in October 1992, and a male child was born to them in December 1993. Earlier, the victim had lodged a first information report alleging cruelty by the accused and had filed a complaint under Sections 107/151 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and a petition seeking maintenance for herself and her child. The victim later returned to the matrimonial home. On 26 September 1994, at about 1:45 a.m., the victim consumed tablets of aluminium phosphide, an insecticide. She was taken to hospital but died at about 5:00 a.m. the same day. The police recorded the death in the daily diary register and sent the body for post-mortem. On 1 October 1994 the victim's brother lodged a first information report alleging that the accused had subjected the victim to cruelty and forced her to commit suicide. After investigation, a chargesheet was filed under Sections 498-A and 306 of the Indian Penal Code. The prosecution relied on the victim's three earlier proceedings against the accused, the fact of poisoning and death, and the fact that the death occurred within seven years of marriage. The accused was said to have told investigators that the victim took the tablets by mistake, believing them to be insecticide, and had not informed the victim's parents immediately after the incident. The defence relied on a suicide note stating the victim acted because of intolerable pain and illness, and on two neighbours who said the couple's relationship was cordial.
offence_severity: Maximum ten years imprisonment and fine (s.306 IPC); no minimum stated in the judgment
physical_harm: Death of the victim from consuming aluminium phosphide tablets; died at hospital the same day
motive: Cruelty and harassment by the accused that drove the victim to suicide (as concurrently found by the trial court and High Court)
key_evidence_accepted: Marriage on 10.10.1992; birth of a male child on 18.12.1993; three cases filed by the victim against the accused (FIR 59/1993, complaint under s.107/151 Cr.P.C., s.125 Cr.P.C. maintenance case); proved poisoning by aluminium phosphide and death; concurrent finding of cruelty under s.498-A
witness_credibility: Two defence neighbour witnesses did not inspire confidence, given the undisputed prior cases filed by the victim; the court made no separate assessment of the victim's brother (PW-3)
post_offence_conduct: Did not inform the victim's parents immediately after the incident; court treated this as indicating guilt. State alleged he tried to mislead the investigation by claiming the tablets were taken by mistake (alleged only)
trial_duration: offence: 26.09.1994; trial judgment: 24.02.2000; High Court: 16.03.2011; Supreme Court: 23 September 2024
legal_representation: Accused: Ashok Tobria, M.S. Yadav, Rajesh Kumar Pandey, S.Y. Usmani and others (Advs.). State: Vikrant Narayan Vasudeva, Sarthak Chiller, Rohit Lochav (Advs.) for the Respondent-State
investigation_status: FIR lodged on 01.10.1994 by victim's brother; investigation completed; chargesheet filed under s.498-A and s.306 IPC; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Suicide note (Exhibit DF) not duly exhibited for admission in evidence
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.498-A, acquitted under s.306. High Court: s.498-A conviction upheld; State's appeal allowed and convicted under s.306. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed, conviction upheld
prosecution_argument: Accused tried to mislead investigation; death within two years of marriage after three complaints by victim; s.113A presumption rightly raised; defence witnesses unconvincing
defence_argument: Settlement of the earlier cases was not an admission of guilt; no cruelty allegations between June 1993 and the death; suicide note shows suicide due to pain and illness; no presumption under s.113A; conviction cannot rest on conjecture and surmise
legal_principle_applied: Section 113A presumption is discretionary and arises only if basic facts (suicide within seven years of marriage and cruelty by husband) are proved; cruelty under s.498-A and abetment under s.306 must be proved beyond reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Hans Raj v. State of Haryana [2004] 2 SCR 676 : (2004) 12 SCC 257; Naresh Kumar v. State of Haryana [2024] 2 SCR 830 : (2024) 3 SCC 573 (s.113A gives discretion, no mandatory presumption)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Victim's three prior cases against the accused for harassment and cruelty; death within seven years of marriage; accused did not inform the victim's parents immediately
